root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Uhlmann Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Be7 4. Nf3 Nf6 5. Bg5 h6 6. Bh4 O-O 7. Rc1 dxc4

overview: After 7.Rc1 dxc4 Black takes the pawn at c4 in a Queen's Gambit Declined with ...h6 inserted, leaving White to recapture and build a central majority. White aims for e3, Bxc4 and a later e4, while Black looks for ...c5 or ...b5 and to trade pieces. Play is solid and strategic.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture with e3 and Bxc4, then e4 if possible
Use the rook on c1 to pressure the c-file

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra c4 pawn briefly to keep space

typical_structures.structure: White centre pawns d4 and e-pawn, Black with symmetrical development after ...dxc4

character.notes: Black's position is hard to break down and play is steady.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn is regained by force.

structure.notes: The centre is in tension and White may play e4 or e3.

level.notes: Strategic ideas matter more than forcing lines.
